Da Nang is not only famous for its beautiful landscapes but also a true culinary paradise filled with irresistible local specialties. This article suggests the most unique and meaningful souvenirs you can bring home from your Da Nang trip in 2026 from beef sausage and dried seafood to traditional handicrafts helping you preserve both the flavors and memories of this charming coastal city.

Da Nang, a beautiful seaside city with soft white sand beaches, crystal-clear waters, and rich cuisine, has long been a favorite destination for travelers. When planning your Da Nang trip in 2026, besides sightseeing and enjoying local food, many visitors wonder what souvenirs to buy for friends and family to capture the spirit and memories of Vietnam’s most livable city. Below is a curated list of distinctive local specialties that make perfect gifts guaranteed to delight the recipients and remind them of the sunny, breezy charm of Central Vietnam. Let’s explore together with Vietlook Travel.

Da Nang Travel 2026: What Souvenirs Best Capture the City’s Flavors and Memories?

Da Nang is renowned not only for iconic landmarks such as the Dragon Bridge, Han River Bridge, and My Khe Beach, but also for its rich culinary heritage. Choosing souvenirs from Da Nang is not simply about buying products it’s about bringing home a piece of local culture and tradition. Each gift tells a story, reflecting the coastal lifestyle, culinary craftsmanship, and cultural identity of Central Vietnam. Below are the most popular and meaningful souvenirs you should consider during your Da Nang journey.

1. Da Nang Beef Sausage – A Traditional Flavor to Remember

Beef sausage (cha bo) is one of the most famous specialties of Da Nang and Central Vietnam. Unlike regular pork sausage, Da Nang beef sausage is made from carefully selected fresh beef, finely ground and seasoned with traditional spices such as pepper, garlic, and premium fish sauce. The mixture is wrapped in fresh banana leaves and steamed, creating a distinctive aroma and firm, chewy texture.

When tasted, the natural sweetness of beef blends perfectly with a mild peppery kick, delivering a memorable flavor. Beef sausage is not only delicious but also an elegant and symbolic gift representing Da Nang cuisine. Choose sausages with a natural light pink color, smooth surface, and a gentle beef aroma. Prices range from 200,000 to 350,000 VND per kilogram. You can buy high-quality beef sausage at Con Market, Han Market, or reputable specialty shops such as Ba Tam or Song Han.

2. One-Sun-Dried Squid – The Essence of the Sea

One-sun-dried squid is a premium seafood delicacy that embodies the essence of Da Nang’s coastal flavor. Fresh squid is dried under the sun for just one day, preserving its natural sweetness, tenderness, and ocean aroma unlike fully dried squid.

When grilled or pan-fried, the squid becomes fragrant, slightly chewy, and irresistibly delicious, making it perfect for family gatherings or casual snacking. One-sun-dried squid is a refined and popular souvenir among travelers. Choose squid with a natural pink color, thick body, and a light white powder on the surface. Prices range from 500,000 to 1,000,000 VND per kilogram. For the best quality, buy from trusted dried seafood stores or fishing villages such as Nam O or Thanh Khe.

3. Tamarind-Rimmed Baby Squid – Sweet and Tangy Delight

Tamarind-rimmed baby squid is a beloved Da Nang specialty, featuring tender baby squid simmered in a sweet-and-sour tamarind sauce. Fresh squid is carefully cleaned and cooked with tamarind juice, sugar, chili, and spices until the sauce thickens and coats each piece evenly.

The result is a flavorful snack with a perfect balance of sweetness, tanginess, and mild spice. This dish is easy to store and transport, making it an ideal souvenir. Prices typically range from 150,000 to 250,000 VND per box and are available at specialty stores and supermarkets.

4. Spicy Dried Filefish – A Savory Snack Favorite

Spicy dried filefish (ca bo kho rim) is another iconic seafood snack from Da Nang. Fresh filefish is dried naturally, then simmered with chili, garlic, sugar, and fish sauce until fully infused with flavor.

With its chewy texture, balanced sweet-salty taste, and spicy kick, this snack is perfect for casual munching or as a gift for seafood lovers. Easy to preserve and carry, dried filefish costs around 180,000–300,000 VND per 500g bag.

5. Nam O Fish Sauce – A Culinary Heritage

Nam O fish sauce is a proud symbol of Da Nang’s traditional cuisine. Produced in the ancient fishing village of Nam O, this fish sauce is made entirely by hand using fresh anchovies and sea salt, fermented naturally in clay jars over many months.

The result is a deep amber-colored sauce with a rich aroma, balanced salinity, and lingering aftertaste. Nam O fish sauce elevates Vietnamese dishes and represents the cultural heritage of coastal Da Nang. Prices range from 80,000 to 150,000 VND per liter, depending on protein content.

6. My Khe Seaweed – A Healthy Gift from the Ocean

Harvested from My Khe Beach one of the most beautiful beaches in the world My Khe seaweed is fresh, nutritious, and rich in minerals. It’s commonly used in soups, salads, and traditional dishes, offering both health benefits and authentic coastal flavor.

Dried My Khe seaweed costs approximately 50,000–100,000 VND per 200g pack and makes an excellent gift for health-conscious friends and family.

7. Peanut Candy – A Sweet Taste of Central Vietnam

Peanut candy is a traditional Central Vietnamese sweet made from roasted peanuts and malt sugar. Crispy, fragrant, and mildly sweet, it pairs perfectly with hot tea and evokes nostalgic childhood memories.

Handmade and affordable, peanut candy is a popular souvenir priced at around 30,000–60,000 VND per pack.

8. Ba Lieu Sesame Crackers – Traditional Culinary Craftsmanship

Ba Lieu sesame crackers are one of Da Nang’s most iconic traditional treats. Made from glutinous rice flour, sugar, ginger, and roasted sesame seeds, the crackers are crispy on the outside and light, aromatic inside, with a subtle gingery warmth.

Priced between 40,000 and 80,000 VND per box, they are a meaningful gift reflecting the craftsmanship and culinary heritage of Da Nang.

9. Specialty Tea and Coffee – Unique Local Beverages

Although not a major tea- or coffee-growing region, Da Nang is a hub for specialty products from nearby areas such as Quang Nam and the Central Highlands. Visitors can find herbal teas, lotus tea, butterfly pea flower tea, and high-quality roasted coffee.

Salt coffee, a unique local variation, offers a fascinating blend of mild saltiness, bitterness, and creamy sweetness. Tea and coffee gifts typically range from 100,000 to 300,000 VND per pack.

10. Handicraft Souvenirs – Cultural Imprints of Da Nang

Beyond food, Da Nang offers a wide range of handicrafts such as hand-painted conical hats, ceramic items, and stone carvings from the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son). These souvenirs reflect local artistry and cultural identity, with prices ranging from a few dollars to several hundred thousand VND depending on craftsmanship.

Smart Shopping Tips for Buying Da Nang Specialties

  • Choose reputable shopping spots: Con Market, Han Market, specialty stores, supermarkets, or airport shops.

  • Check packaging and expiration dates, especially for food products.

  • Bargain politely at traditional markets.

  • Buy moderate quantities and request vacuum sealing for dried seafood.

  • Ask locals for recommendations to find the best quality products.

  • Shop early in the morning for the freshest goods.

  • Consider transport conditions, especially for items requiring refrigeration.

Central Vietnamese cuisine, especially Da Nang’s, is incredibly diverse and appealing. This curated list by Vietlook Travel will help you choose meaningful and delicious souvenirs for your loved ones. We hope these suggestions make your Da Nang trip even more fulfilling and memorable. Happy travels and enjoy discovering the flavors of Da Nang.
